title: Durmitor Ridges
subRegion: Durmitor National Park & Žabljak, northern Montenegro

bestPeriod.avoid: November-May (Sedlo pass road snow-blocked, high ridges unrunnable, Žabljak is a ski town); late July-August has the crowds and afternoon storms

accommodation.note: Žabljak guesthouses €35, €70 dbl/night; Škrka mountain hut ~€15, €20

food.note: Main course €7, €12; a full dinner with rakija under €20

transport.note: Rental car 7 days €180, €280, fuel, Sozina/Tara tolls

activities.note: NP daily entry ~€5, or the all-parks card ~€13.50; Tara rafting half-day €40, €55

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5-1,000-1,400 m days on sharp karst with short exposed scrambles; no glacier, but very little forgiving ground

gatewayAirport: TGD, Podgorica (2 h-2 h 30 drive to Žabljak via Nikšić or the Tara bridge); TIV, Tivat is 2 h 45
summary: Durmitor is a compact, savage limestone massif with 48 peaks over 2,000 m packed into an area you can drive across in forty minutes, and Žabljak at 1,456 m is the highest town in the Balkans, which means you sleep at altitude and start every run from a car park rather than a valley. The rock is pale, fluted karst with almost no soil, so the running is fast on the grass shelves and genuinely sharp on the ridges. The week arcs from a lake-circuit warm-up through the two showpiece summits, Bobotov Kuk and Prutaš, into a two-day Škrčka lakes excursion with a hut night, then a recovery day on the Tara canyon rim and a fast finish on Savin Kuk. It suits runners who like empty mountains, do not need refuge comfort, and can carry their own water.

itinerary.title: Drive up from Podgorica, warm up at Crno jezero
itinerary.morning: Land at TGD, collect the car, drive north through the Moraća canyon and over to **Žabljak (1,456 m)**, 2 h to 2 h 30 depending on route. Buy the national park ticket at the Crno jezero booth or the visitor centre.
itinerary.afternoon: Shake out on the **Crno jezero (Black Lake) circuit**, 3.6 km around both basins on flat forest track, then add the gentle climb to the **Zminje jezero** for another 4 km. Enough to feel the altitude, not enough to cost anything.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Žabljak, cicvara, kajmak and lamb ispod sača at one of the town's konobas; wash it down with a local Vranac.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 220 m D+ / T1 / 55 min-1 h 15; drive 2 h-2 h 30; NP entry ~€5.

itinerary.title: Prutaš, the slab mountain
itinerary.morning: Drive the **P14 road to Sedlo pass (1,907 m)**, 25 minutes from Žabljak, and park at the col. Run the ridge south-west to **Prutaš (2,393 m)**, grass shelves, then the famous banded limestone strata tilted like the pages of a book.
itinerary.afternoon: Return over Sedlo and add the short spur north toward **Velika Previja** for the first sight of the Škrka cirque and Bobotov's south face. Back to Žabljak by mid-afternoon.
itinerary.evening: Beer on the Žabljak main street; early dinner and a properly early night before tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.2 km / 560 m D+ / T2-T3 / 1 h 30-2 h / high point 2,393 m / no water above Žabljak.

itinerary.title: Bobotov Kuk, 2,523 m
itinerary.morning: Leave Žabljak at 06:15 for Sedlo. Climb the scree gully and the traverse to **Velika Previja**, then the cabled, exposed final ridge onto **Bobotov Kuk (2,523 m)**, the classic Durmitor summit, with the whole Tara canyon system on one side and Bosnian ranges on the other.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend by the same route to Sedlo, or, if fit, take the long variant down to **Lokvice katun** and out via Ivan Do to Žabljak, refilling at the katun spring and buying cheese from the shepherds.
itinerary.evening: Recovery meal in Žabljak; a soak in the hotel wellness if it has one.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.9 km / 940 m D+ (or 19 km / 1,450 m by Lokvice) / T3 with cables / 2 h 15-3 h / 2 L water minimum.

itinerary.title: Down into the Škrka cirque, hut night
itinerary.morning: Sedlo again, but this time run north-west over **Velika Previja** and drop into the **Škrka cirque**, a 500 m descent on loose karst steps into the most isolated bowl in the park, holding **Veliko and Malo Škrčko jezero** at about 1,686 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy exploration of the two lakes and the surrounding pastures, then check into the **Škrka mountain hut**, basic, bunk-bed, hot food, and the only building for hours in any direction.
itinerary.evening: Hut dinner and one of the darkest night skies in Europe; the cirque walls block every light source.

itinerary.title: Climb out, then a genuine recovery afternoon on the Tara rim
itinerary.morning: Reverse the climb out of the cirque to Sedlo, 550 m up, taken slowly as the only hard effort of the day, and drive back to Žabljak.
itinerary.afternoon: True low day. An easy 7 km jog out to the **Ćurevac viewpoint (1,625 m)** on soft forest track for the head-on view 1,300 m down into the **Tara canyon**, the deepest in Europe. Then coffee and nothing else.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Žabljak; plan the last two days around the forecast.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km out / 550 m D+, then 7 km / 300 m D+ / total ~1 h 50 running / Tara canyon depth ~1,300 m.

itinerary.title: Savin Kuk and the Tara river
itinerary.morning: From Crno jezero, climb **Savin Kuk (2,313 m)** on the ski-area flank and the summit ridge, a shorter, less committing summit than Bobotov with an equally complete panorama over the Žabljak plateau and the Piva side.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to the **Đurđevića Tara bridge** and take a half-day raft on the Tara, cold, fast, green water at the bottom of the canyon you looked into yesterday. The best possible active recovery.
itinerary.evening: Grilled trout and rakija at a riverside restaurant near the bridge.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 900 m D+ / T2-T3 / 2 h-2 h 45; rafting €40, €55 half-day; 35 min drive to the bridge.

itinerary.title: Katun loop and the drive out
itinerary.morning: Last run: the **Ivan Do-Lokvice katun** loop from Crno jezero, up through black pine to the shepherds' summer settlement at about 1,800 m and back on the Zminje side, the most characteristic Durmitor ground, all pasture, karst pavement and sheep bells.
itinerary.afternoon: Buy cheese and honey in Žabljak, then the drive south to Podgorica, ideally via the **Tara bridge and the Piva canyon** if the flight allows.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km / 700 m D+ / 2 h-2 h 30; drive to TGD 2 h-2 h 30.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Soa
accommodationStrategy.description: The pragmatic town base: five minutes' drive from the Crno jezero park entrance and the P14 Sedlo road, parking, a proper breakfast, and staff who will do an early one if you ask the night before. Good value at €55, €90 double in shoulder season, and it has drying space, which matters when Durmitor weather turns.

accommodationStrategy.name: Planinarski dom Škrka
accommodationStrategy.description: The only accommodation inside the high massif and the reason Day 4 works. Bunks, a stove, simple hot food and no electricity to speak of, bring cash, a sleeping bag liner and a headtorch. Confirm it is staffed before you commit to descending into the cirque; outside high summer it may be locked.

accommodationStrategy.name: Guesthouse or apartman in Ivan Do
accommodationStrategy.description: The runner's alternative: apartments a kilometre from the Crno jezero trailhead, €35, €55 a night, with a kitchen for early breakfasts and late dinners. Ideal if you want to start on foot rather than driving to the lake each morning.

logistics.connectivity: Montenegro is **not** in the EU, but it participates in the Western Balkans roaming arrangement and most EU operators now apply reduced or roam-like-at-home terms, check your tariff, and consider a local Telekom/One prepaid SIM. **No signal in the Škrka cirque, the Tara canyon floor, or the deep forest bowls.**
logistics.emergency: **112**; mountain rescue in Montenegro is run by the Gorska služba spašavanja (GSS) and is volunteer-based, so response is slower than in the Alps. Helicopter availability is limited. Carry insurance with mountain cover and repatriation, and leave your route with your accommodation.
logistics.weather: Durmitor makes its own weather. Violent afternoon thunderstorms from mid-June through August, often building from 13:00; sudden temperature drops of 15 °C; and snow possible on the ridges in any month. The massif also catches Adriatic fronts, which arrive fast from the south-west. Check the Montenegrin hydrometeorological service each morning.
logistics.bookingWindows: Žabljak beds are plentiful except in the first three weeks of August, 2-4 weeks ahead is enough otherwise. The **Škrka hut** should be confirmed by phone through the Žabljak visitor centre a few days ahead. Tara rafting books same-day outside August. Rental cars for August need months.
logistics.money: **Montenegro uses the euro** although it is not in the eurozone. Cards work in hotels and larger restaurants in Žabljak; **the national park booth, the hut, katuns and small konobas are cash-only**, bring €200 in small notes. Tipping: round up, 10% for a good meal.
logistics.transportRules: A rental car is essentially required, buses reach Žabljak but nothing inside the park. Montenegro has no vignette; the **Sozina tunnel** on the coast route is tolled (a few euros). Check that your rental agreement permits the unpaved sections; the P14 to Sedlo is paved but narrow and gated by snow into June. Green Card insurance is needed to cross into Bosnia for the Piva loop.
logistics.permits: **Durmitor National Park charges a daily entry fee of roughly €5 per person**, collected at Crno jezero and other entry points; an all-parks annual card is around €13.50 and pays for itself in three days. No running permit needed. Wild camping is restricted to designated areas; drones need park permission. Do not disturb katun livestock or leave gates open.
logistics.health: Žabljak tap water is potable; treat all lake and stream water. **Nose-horned viper (poskok)** is present on sunny karst below 1,800 m, Europe's most venomous snake, though bites are rare; wear proper shoes and don't put hands blind onto ledges. Ticks in the pine and beech forest. Karst edges are sharp and undercut: a slip on Bobotov's summit block is a serious injury, not a graze.

proTips: **Buy the all-parks card, not day tickets.** At roughly €13.50 against ~€5 a day, it pays back on day three and also covers Biogradska Gora and Lovćen if you drive out via the coast.

**Do Bobotov Kuk from Sedlo, not from Crno jezero, on your first attempt.** The Sedlo start saves 500 m of climbing and puts you on the summit two hours earlier, which on a storm day is the whole safety margin.

**Refill at Lokvice katun and buy the cheese.** The shepherds' summer settlement is the only reliable water between Žabljak and the high ridges, and the sheep's cheese and kajmak sold there is better than anything in town.
**Check the Sedlo road before you plan the week.** The P14 over Sedlo is the key to three of the seven days and it can stay snow-blocked into mid-June and close early after an autumn storm.
**Descend into Škrka in the morning, never the afternoon.** The climb out is 500 m on loose karst with no water and no phone signal; doing it in evening light or a storm is the classic Durmitor epic.
**Run Prutaš in low side-light.** The banded strata that make the mountain famous only read properly early or late, mid-morning flattens them completely.
**Use the Tara raft as your recovery session.** Half a day of cold water and no impact after a Bobotov day does more for your legs than a rest morning in the hotel.
**Watch the sheepdogs at the katuns.** Šarplaninac guard dogs work loose around the summer settlements. Stop running, walk, and wait for a shepherd, never try to outrun one.

raw.Signature routes: (1) **Bobotov Kuk (2,523 m) from Sedlo pass (1,907 m)**: 9.9 km out-and-back, 940 m D+, mid-pack run 2 h 15-3 h (hiking guides quote 5 h 30). (2) **Bobotov Kuk the long way from Crno jezero** via Ivan Do, Lokvice katun and Velika Previja: 19 km, 1,450 m D+, 4 h-5 h 30. (3) **Prutaš (2,393 m) from Sedlo**: 8.2 km out-and-back, 560 m D+, 1 h 30-2 h, the most photogenic striated slabs in the Balkans. (4) **Škrčka jezera (1,686 m) circuit from Sedlo** down the Škrka cirque and back over Velika Previja: 17 km, 1,100 m D+, 3 h-4 h. (5) **Savin Kuk (2,313 m) from Crno jezero**: 12 km, 900 m D+, 2 h-2 h 45. (6) **Crno jezero circuit**: 3.6 km, 60 m D+, 22-30 min. (7) **Ćurevac (1,625 m) Tara rim** from Tepca road: 7 km, 300 m D+, 50 min-1 h 10.
raw.Technicality (SAC hiking scale T1-T5, st: Crno jezero circuit **T1**. Prutaš and Savin Kuk **T2-T3**. Bobotov Kuk **T3**, with a cabled section and about 80 m of easy but genuinely exposed scrambling on the summit block, plus a steep scree gully on the Sedlo side. Škrka descent **T3** on loose karst steps. Nothing needs a rope, but Bobotov Kuk in the wet is a different mountain, the polished limestone becomes lethal.
raw.Terrain split, week average: ~40% bare fluted karst and limestone slab, ~20% scree and gully, ~15% high grass shelf and katun pasture (the only genuinely fast ground), ~15% black-pine and beech forest singletrack around the lakes, ~10% gravel park track. The karst is razor-edged: it shreds soft uppers and destroys hands in a fall, so long shoes with a rock plate and light gloves are sensible.
raw.Waymarking: Balkan standard **red circle with a white dot**, plus numbered wooden posts installed by the national park and the Via Dinarica **White Trail** (a "VD" white blaze) crossing the massif. Marking is good on the main peaks and thin in the Škrka cirque, where cairns take over. Timings on posts are hiking times, halve them.
raw.Water refill points and month reliabilit: Durmitor is porous karst and **water is the planning constraint**. Reliable: **Žabljak town taps and the Crno jezero café**, all season; **Lokvice katun spring** (shepherds' summer settlement below Bobotov Kuk), reliable while the katun is occupied, roughly **mid-June to mid-September**, dry outside it; **Škrčka jezera** lake water and the hut at Škrka, treat or ask the hut; **Crno jezero** itself, treat. **Nothing at all at Sedlo pass, on Prutaš, on the Bobotov ridge or on the Ćurevac rim.** Snow patches in the north gullies give melt into early July and nothing after. Carry 2 L on any Sedlo day.
raw.Navigation: The Durmitor 1:25,000 hiking map sold at the NP visitor centre in Žabljak is the standard; GPX from the Via Dinarica portal, Wikiloc and Komoot. Coverage: reasonable in Žabljak and on ridges, **dead in the Škrka cirque, in the Tara canyon below the rim and in the Zminje/Crno forest bowls**. Bail-outs: from Bobotov Kuk, back to Sedlo (fastest) or down to Lokvice and Ivan Do; from Škrka, the Škrka hut is the only shelter and the exit is a 500 m climb, do not descend into that cirque late in the day.
raw.Recovery, altitude and heat: Day 5 is a real low day on the Tara rim. Working altitude 1,900-2,520 m from a 1,456 m base, so no acclimatisation problem but noticeably thinner air on the Bobotov scramble. Convective storms build over the massif from about 13:00 in July and are severe, the ridges are the highest ground for a long way and lightning strikes here are not theoretical. Be off Bobotov Kuk by early afternoon, every time.

sources.verified: Durmitor National Park entry is charged per person per day at approximately €5, with a Montenegro all-national-parks card around €13.50; the Bobotov Kuk out-and-back from Sedlo is about 9.9 km with roughly 939 m of ascent and the Sedlo trailhead is around a 25-minute drive from Žabljak on the P14; Montenegro uses the euro without being in the eurozone.
sources.confidenceNotes: Re-verify (a) **the current Durmitor entry fee and card price**, which the park revises; (b) **Škrka mountain hut staffing, opening dates, price and booking channel**, it is the single most volatile item in this itinerary and should be confirmed by phone before Day 4 is committed; (c) **P14 Sedlo pass road opening date** for the travel month, which depends entirely on snow clearance; (d) **Ćurevac viewpoint access**, the approach road has been closed or restricted in some seasons for erosion; (e) **Montenegro roaming terms** for the traveller's specific EU operator; (f) named Žabljak restaurants and hotel price bands, which turn over frequently.
